case.title: Valid recovery opens dedicated new-password view
case.identity: Same confirmed test account shown in the current recovery request screenshot
case.link: Reset password in the newest recovery email already received; never shared or persisted
case.if_already_opened: Keep the existing result page and report it; do not reopen the email link.
case.browser_context: Use the same private browser window as the recovery request, with a new tab there if needed.
case.expected_identity: Verified account matches the intended recovery account
owner_return_fields: Whether the loaded address ends with auth.html?flow=recover without a token/code or fragment
case.error_or_wrong_identity: Stop and report the displayed message; do not resend, reopen or save.

source_review.auth-flows.js: Recovery init uses the isolated Auth client, verifies the link, shows the verified identity, sets Choose a new password and exposes the two-password form. It does not save a password, require an application proof or adopt the normal app session just by opening this view.
source_review.auth-security.js: consumeAuthUrl captures and removes link material before asynchronous work. createLinkController.verify requires actual recovery link material and a remotely verified confirmed Auth user; it does not fall back to an existing session for a missing link.
source_review.auth.html: Dedicated securityPassword form has New password, Repeat new password and Save password. Saving is a later action.

expected_Auth_session_effect: Opening consumes the one-use recovery link and establishes the isolated recovery Auth session. No password change is requested; keep the loaded page available for the next handoff.
later_password_save_readiness: Password save can invalidate existing approvals/proofs. Confirm the controlled gateway code recipient and bounded application-window readiness before a separate save/verification/continuation step.
